title: Markup.io vs BugHerd
kicker: · MARKUP.IO VS BUGHERD · COMPARED FOR AGENCIES
headline: Markup.io vs BugHerd: which fits your agency?
standfirst: Both let a client comment free from a link, no account. The fork: Markup.io renders the site through its own proxy so you can comment on live pages, PDFs, and 30-plus file types in one place. BugHerd pins straight onto the live page itself and manages the work on a built-in kanban board.
disclosure: We make Superflow, a third option in this space. It appears once, at the end, clearly marked. Everything above it is a straight comparison.
dateline: Facts checked July 2026, from markup.io and bugherd.com.
shortAnswerPickLeft: if you review websites, PDFs, images, and video in one place, and want a flat price with unlimited internal users.
shortAnswerPickRight: if you want pins to live directly on the page with browser, OS, and screen size attached, and a built-in kanban board to run the work.
shortAnswerShared: Both assume a person finds every mistake.

dimensions.label: Who checks the site
dimensions.framing: Start with the question everything else depends on.
leftFacts: A person checks it. Nothing checks the site automatically.
No AI features found on markup.io's product, pricing, or docs pages, checked July 2026.
rightFacts: A person finds every issue, then pins it.
dimensions.verdict: Even. In both tools, the checking is a person's job. That is the premise the third option removes.

dimensions.label: How the client says yes
dimensions.framing: Both make commenting easy. Only one has a named sign-off step.
leftFacts: Guests comment free from a link, no signup required.
Statuses plus a per-reviewer Sign off flow: Open for review, Editing content, On hold, Completed. Only Admins and owners set status.
rightFacts: Guests comment free from a link, no account.
A formal approval flow: not yet verified.
dimensions.verdict: Comment collection: even, both good, both free for guests. A named sign-off step: Markup.io, with its Statuses and per-reviewer Sign off flow.

dimensions.label: Where you review
dimensions.framing: On the live page, or on a rendering of it.
leftFacts: Proxy and iFrame rendering of the live URL, pins keyed to URL and query string.
Chrome extension is optional and helps on authenticated or iFrame-blocked sites. Behind-login support is partial.
rightFacts: Element pins on the live page itself, with browser, OS, and screen size attached.
Behind-login or authenticated-site behavior: not yet verified.
dimensions.verdict: Direct on-page pinning, no proxy step: BugHerd. Markup.io's proxy and iFrame rendering can break on login-gated or iFrame-blocking sites unless the Chrome extension or a temporary auth change helps.

dimensions.label: What stays private
dimensions.framing: Your team needs somewhere to disagree.
leftFacts: Private MarkUps make a whole MarkUp private, a different concept.
Internal or private comments the client cannot see: not yet verified.
rightFacts: Private or internal comments: not yet verified.
dimensions.verdict: Even: not yet verified on either side. Markup.io's Private MarkUps controls a whole document, not a per-comment internal note, so it does not resolve the question either.

dimensions.label: What gets captured
dimensions.framing: Both tools pin. The difference is what gets attached without asking.
leftFacts: Chrome extension auto-captures a screenshot on every comment or pin.
Auto screenshots without the extension: not yet verified.
Native video or screen recording: not yet verified. Loom integration attaches video.
rightFacts: Browser, OS, and screen size attach to every pin, no extension needed.
Automatic per-comment screenshots: not yet verified.
dimensions.verdict: BugHerd. Browser, OS, and screen size attach natively to every pin, and video feedback ships in the product. Markup.io's auto-screenshot is verified with the Chrome extension; without it, not yet verified.

dimensions.label: What it remembers
dimensions.framing: Does project ten start smarter than project one?
leftFacts: No per-client memory or knowledge concept found in docs: not yet verified.
rightFacts: No memory concept. Each project starts blank, checked July 2026.
dimensions.verdict: Even: neither. BugHerd's absence is confirmed by the vendor; Markup.io's is not yet verified, but no such feature turned up in its docs either.

dimensions.label: How it fits your stack
dimensions.framing: One goes wide on automation. One goes deep on the board.
leftFacts: Workspaces, Folders, and Statuses on a dashboard. No kanban found.
Native Slack, Microsoft Teams, Loom, and Zapier (5,000-plus apps), plus a public API with webhooks.
Zapier flows run outbound, with MarkUp as the trigger app, alongside the API and webhooks. Native two-way sync with a PM tool: not yet verified.
rightFacts: Built-in kanban board. The tool is the workspace.
Integrations: Jira, Trello, Asana, ClickUp, Slack, Teams.
dimensions.verdict: Board-first studio: BugHerd, with its kanban built in. Automation reach: Markup.io, with Zapier, a public API, and webhooks, though its verified Zapier flows run outbound. Neither wins outright; it depends on whether your team needs a board or a pipe.

dimensions.label: What it costs
dimensions.framing: The sticker and the math are different numbers.
leftFacts: Pro: $79 per month, flat, unlimited users (admins, members, guests), 1 Workspace, 500GB storage, 100MB attachment cap.
Enterprise custom, with SSO (SAML) and SOC II. Free tier after a 14-day trial, capped at 5 MarkUps and 10GB. Guests free, no page-view caps advertised.
rightFacts: Standard $50, Studio $80, Premium $150 per month, for 5, 10, and 25 members. Plus $8 per extra member.
Enterprise custom, with SSO. Guests free, no page-view caps advertised.
dimensions.verdict: Smaller teams: BugHerd Standard at $50 undercuts Markup.io's flat $79. Past about ten internal seats, Markup.io wins outright, since its $79 already covers unlimited users while BugHerd's per-member add-on keeps climbing.

pricingNote: Both columns verified July 2026. Markup.io Pro is $79 a month flat, unlimited admins, members, and guests, 1 Workspace, 500GB storage, 100MB attachments. BugHerd runs Standard $50 for 5 members, Studio $80 for 10, Premium $150 for 25, plus $8 per extra member. The agency math: at 5 internal seats BugHerd's $50 undercuts Markup.io's $79. At 10 seats the two are close, $80 against $79. Past 10 seats Markup.io's flat price wins outright, since BugHerd keeps adding $8 per member. Guests are free and unlimited on both, and neither advertises a page-view cap.
thirdOptionBody: Both Markup.io and BugHerd assume a person finds every mistake. Superflow is a QA tool + a team: AI agents built from your checklist check every site change, your team decides, your client approves from a link.

faq.question: Which is better for a small agency?
faq.answer: Markup.io if you review websites, PDFs, images, and video in one place with a flat price; BugHerd if you want pins directly on the page and a built-in kanban board.

faq.question: Do clients need accounts?
faq.answer: No on both. Guests comment free from a share link on Markup.io and BugHerd alike, no signup required.

faq.question: Which is cheaper?
faq.answer: For a handful of internal seats, BugHerd Standard at $50 undercuts Markup.io's flat $79. Past about ten seats, Markup.io's unlimited-user price wins, since BugHerd adds $8 per extra member.

faq.question: Can either check the site itself?
faq.answer: No. Both collect what a person found. BugHerd ships no AI, and no AI features were found on markup.io's product, pricing, or docs pages as of July 2026. That's the third option above.

faq.question: Does either tool work behind a client's login?
faq.answer: Markup.io's behind-login support is partial: its proxy and iFrame rendering can break unless the Chrome extension or a temporary auth change helps. BugHerd's behind-login behavior is not yet verified.
